//: Composite indexes Firestore cannot infer.
Firestore indexes single fields automatically. It does NOT index a query
that combines several equality filters with an orderBy on a different
field — that needs a composite index declared ahead of time, and until
one exists the query throws FAILED_PRECONDITION at runtime.
This file exists so that requirement is reviewable in a pull request
rather than a console click somebody has to remember. Adding a query of
that shape without adding it here is a deploy that works locally against
the emulator and fails in production.
Deploy:  firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes
There is no firebase.json in this repo, so that command needs one (or
`firebase init firestore` once). The equivalent by hand is Firestore >
Indexes > Composite > Add, with the fields below in this exact order —
order is part of the index, not a presentation detail.
Building an index over an existing collection is not instant. Expect
'Building' for a few minutes on a small collection; the query keeps
failing until it flips to 'Enabled'.
GET /api/billing/license — grantingOrder().
Finds the most recent purchase that carries a given plan, so the
certificate can print a licence id and an issue date, and derive the
twelve-month update window from it.
The route catches the failure and returns the certificate with
licenseId: null rather than 500ing, which is the right behaviour and
also the reason this is easy to miss: without the index nothing
breaks visibly, every customer simply gets a certificate with the one
field on it that a procurement inbox actually asks for left blank.
createdAt is DESCENDING because the query takes limit(1) off the top
to mean 'most recent'. An ascending index does not serve it.
